GAR-Dongre also rises (0.019$\to$0.353; $N$\,=\,5 pilot)---the only intervention that moves both attention metrics. The benefit diminishes in longer dialogues (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), consistent with exposure bias compounding over turns.

56	\subsection{Scheduled Sampling Compresses the TF--AR Gap}\label{subsec:ss}
57	
58	If exposure bias is the root cause (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}), reducing the training-inference distribution mismatch should narrow the gap. Scheduled sampling \citep{bengio2015scheduled}---mixing model-generated tokens into training prefixes with linearly increasing probability---directly targets this mismatch.
59	
60	Across three seeds, AR GAR-ours rises from 0.064 to $0.401\pm0.047$ (seeds: 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.433), compressing the gap from 7.8$\times$ to ${\sim}$1.3$\times$ with no PPL cost ($1.441\pm0.001$).\footnote{Seed 123 TF GAR unavailable (checkpoint error); per-seed gaps: 1.45$\times$ (s42), 1.15$\times$ (s456).} Steering on SS models is remarkably stable across seeds ($\beta$\,=\,5: $0.717\pm0.001$). GAR-Dongre also rises (0.019$\to$0.353; $N$\,=\,5 pilot)---the only intervention that moves both metrics. The benefit diminishes in longer dialogues (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), consistent with exposure bias compounding over turns.
61

57	
58	If exposure bias is the root cause (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}), reducing the training-inference distribution mismatch should narrow the gap. Scheduled sampling \citep{bengio2015scheduled}---mixing model-generated tokens into training prefixes with linearly increasing probability---directly targets this mismatch.
59	
60	Across three seeds, AR GAR-ours rises from 0.064 to $0.401\pm0.047$ (seeds: 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.433), compressing the gap from 7.8$\times$ to ${\sim}$1.3$\times$ with no PPL cost ($1.441\pm0.001$).\footnote{Seed 123 TF GAR unavailable (checkpoint error); per-seed gaps: 1.45$\times$ (s42), 1.15$\times$ (s456).} Steering on SS models is remarkably stable across seeds ($\beta$\,=\,5: $0.717\pm0.001$)---the training-time seed variance (std\,=\,0.047 at $\beta$\,=\,0) is nearly eliminated by inference-time steering, suggesting that $\beta$-steering converges to a seed-independent attention equilibrium. GAR-Dongre also rises (0.019$\to$0.353; $N$\,=\,5 pilot)---the only intervention that moves both metrics. The benefit diminishes in longer dialogues (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), consistent with exposure bias compounding over turns.
61	
62

44	\end{figure}
45	
46	\subsection{Inference-Time Attention Steering}\label{subsec:steering}
47	
48	All training-time interventions leave the exposure bias gap intact. If the collapse is caused by attention misallocation rather than representation degradation, then directly correcting attention should recover GAR. We test this by adding a constant bias $\beta$ to pre-softmax attention logits for goal-token positions during generation:
49	\begin{equation}
50	  \tilde{A}_{i,j}^{(\ell,h)} = A_{i,j}^{(\ell,h)} + \beta \cdot \mathbf{1}[j \in \mathcal{G}],
51	\end{equation}
52	where $\tilde{A}$ denotes the modified logits before softmax. The additive form operates in log-probability space, providing uniform boost even when baseline attention is near zero (Figure~\ref{fig:headline}b). The response is sharply nonlinear: $\beta \in [0, 2]$ yields marginal improvement, then $\beta = 3$ triggers a phase transition to GAR\,=\,0.556 (9\% PPL cost). At $\beta$\,=\,5, GAR reaches 0.727$\pm$0.061 (PPL 1.77); the operating region $\beta \in [3, 5]$ exceeds the TF baseline while PPL remains below 1.8 (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-steering}).
53	
54	This closes the causal loop: if the collapse were due to representation drift in hidden states, no amount of attention reweighting could recover GAR. The recovery confirms attention misallocation---not representation degradation---as the proximal cause.
55	
56	\subsection{Scheduled Sampling Compresses the TF--AR Gap}\label{subsec:ss}
57	
58	If exposure bias is the root cause (\S\ref{subsec:dist-shift}), reducing the training-inference distribution mismatch should narrow the gap. Scheduled sampling \citep{bengio2015scheduled}---mixing model-generated tokens into training prefixes with linearly increasing probability---directly targets this mismatch.
59	
60	Across three seeds, AR GAR-ours rises from 0.064 to $0.401\pm0.047$ (seeds: 0.347 / 0.423 / 0.433), compressing the gap from 7.8$\times$ to ${\sim}$1.3$\times$ with no PPL cost ($1.441\pm0.001$).\footnote{Seed 123 TF GAR unavailable (checkpoint error); per-seed gaps: 1.45$\times$ (s42), 1.15$\times$ (s456).} Steering on SS models is remarkably stable across seeds ($\beta$\,=\,5: $0.717\pm0.001$)---the training-time seed variance (std\,=\,0.047 at $\beta$\,=\,0) is nearly eliminated by inference-time steering, suggesting that $\beta$-steering converges to a seed-independent attention equilibrium. GAR-Dongre also rises (0.019$\to$0.353; $N$\,=\,5 pilot)---the only intervention that moves both metrics. The benefit diminishes in longer dialogues (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-n5}), consistent with exposure bias compounding over turns.
61

1	\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	The failure traces to an incompatibility between teacher-forcing and GAR-family auxiliary losses, not to the gating architecture. This has implications beyond ThreadGate: any auxiliary attention objective paired with teacher forcing---whether per-head gating \citep{qiu2025gated}, split-softmax \citep{li2024measuring}, or residual scaling \citep{bachlechner2021rezero}---should face the same exposure bias barrier when targeting distributional properties of the attention pattern rather than the prediction itself.
4	
5	\paragraph{Why NTP self-recovers but GAR does not.} NTP self-recovers because the task---predict one token from a prefix---is identical at training and inference; exposure bias shifts the prefix distribution but preserves the prediction task \citep{he2019exposure}. GAR optimizes a \emph{global property of the prefix}---attention allocation to goal tokens---that has no autoregressive counterpart: the model receives no feedback on attention distributions during generation, so the training signal is specific to teacher-forced prefixes.
6	
7	\paragraph{Downstream effects.} Instruction retention ($\beta$\,=\,3) shows late-turn compliance rising from 75.9\% to 87.0\% (+11.1\,pp, McNemar $p$\,=\,0.077; GAR correlation $r$\,=\,0.200, $p$\,=\,0.007). Content constraints benefit most (+23.8\,pp), while format constraints show zero change---consistent with GAR targeting cross-turn semantic coherence rather than locally-verifiable procedural rules (Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix-ir}).
8	
9	\paragraph{SS and steering as substitutes.} Scheduled sampling provides training-time mitigation with no inference cost ($\beta$\,=\,0); steering provides inference-time recovery with PPL cost. At high $\beta$, steering dominates and the two converge---they are substitutes, not complements ($\beta$\,=\,5: SS GAR\,=\,$0.717\pm0.001$ vs.\ TG GAR\,=\,0.727; Figure~\ref{fig:headline}b). The practical choice depends on the acceptable inference-time overhead: SS is preferable when inference budgets are tight, steering when retraining is infeasible.

\section{Scheduled Sampling Implementation}\label{sec:appendix-ss}

Our scheduled sampling implementation follows \citet{bengio2015scheduled} with modifications for multi-turn transformer training:

\paragraph{Sampling schedule.} The model-generated context ratio $\rho$ increases linearly from 0 to 0.3 over 3 epochs. At each training step, a Bernoulli trial with probability $\rho$ determines whether the input prefix is replaced with model-generated tokens. The effective usage rate (29.7--37.1\%) is lower than the nominal schedule due to per-sample Bernoulli variance.

\paragraph{Context generation.} When model-generated context is selected, the model autoregressively generates the assistant turns from the conversation prefix up to the current training position. The generated tokens replace the ground-truth assistant tokens in the input, while user turns remain unchanged. This preserves the multi-turn structure while introducing distributional diversity in the conditioning context.

\paragraph{Training dynamics.} The scheduled sampling variant converges to similar final loss (NTP 0.932 vs.\ 0.930 for standard ThreadGate) but with higher variance in early epochs due to the stochastic context mixing. Gate profiles remain similar (mean 0.953 vs.\ 0.947, min at L4 vs.\ L1), indicating that scheduled sampling does not fundamentally alter gate optimization but rather improves the robustness of the learned attention patterns to distributional shift. Training time increases by 8--80\% across seeds (seed-dependent; dominated by GAR forward pass overhead): 6.5h (seed 42) and 10.8h (seed 123) vs.\ 6.0h for standard ThreadGate on Qwen.

\section{Computational Cost Analysis}\label{sec:appendix-cost}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering\small
\caption{Computational cost across training configurations. All experiments use a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (102\,GB VRAM).}
\label{tab:cost}
\resizebox{\columnwidth}{!}{%
\begin{tabular}{lcccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Config} & \textbf{Params} & \textbf{Time (h)} & \textbf{VRAM} & \textbf{Overhead} \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{l}{\emph{Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct}} \\
LoRA-only & 4.2M & 6.0 & 42\,GB & baseline \\
ThreadGate & 4.3M & 6.0 & 43\,GB & $+$57K \\
\;+\,PCGrad & 4.3M & 8.0 & 43\,GB & $+$33\% \\
Uniform Gate & 4.3M & 6.0 & 43\,GB & $+$57K \\
SS (s42) & 4.3M & 6.5 & 43\,GB & $+$8\% \\
SS (s123) & 4.3M & 10.8 & 43\,GB & $+$80\% \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{5}{l}{\emph{Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct}} \\
LoRA-only & 4.2M & 7.0 & 45\,GB & baseline \\
ThreadGate & 4.3M & 7.3 & 46\,GB & $+$65K \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}}
\end{table}

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import os

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'DejaVu Sans',
    'font.size': 9,
    'axes.titlesize': 10,
    'axes.labelsize': 9,
    'xtick.labelsize': 8,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'legend.fontsize': 7.5,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.05,
    'axes.spines.top': False,
    'axes.spines.right': False,
    'pdf.fonttype': 42,
    'ps.fonttype': 42,
    'lines.linewidth': 1.5,
})

C_BASE = '#BAB0AC'
C_TG   = '#E15759'
C_SS   = '#59A14F'
C_LORA = '#4E79A7'
C_UG   = '#F28E2B'
C_PCG  = '#EDC948'

turns = np.arange(1, 6)
data = {
    'Base':      ([0.0853, 0.0319, 0.0206, 0.0125, 0.0042], C_BASE, 's', '--'),
    'LoRA-only': ([0.1072, 0.0586, 0.0304, 0.0489, 0.0397], C_LORA, 'D', '-'),
    'PCGrad':    ([0.0903, 0.0382, 0.0276, 0.0292, 0.0267], C_PCG,  '^', '-'),
    'UG':        ([0.1130, 0.0564, 0.0328, 0.0198, 0.0160], C_UG,   'v', '-'),
    'TG':        ([0.1297, 0.0725, 0.0591, 0.0428, 0.0664], C_TG,   'o', '-'),
    'SS':        ([0.5264, 0.4494, 0.4380, 0.3996, 0.3909], C_SS,   'P', '-'),
}

bar_data = {
    'Base':      0.0186,
    'LoRA-only': 0.0373,
    'PCGrad':    0.0301,
    'UG':        0.0333,
    'TG':        0.0641,
    'SS':        0.4231,
}

outdir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Plot 1: Per-turn AR GAR curves
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.0, 2.8))

for name, (vals, col, mk, ls) in data.items():
    ax.plot(turns, vals, linestyle=ls, marker=mk, color=col,
            markersize=5, markerfacecolor=col, markeredgecolor='white',
            markeredgewidth=0.6, label=name, zorder=3)

ax.set_xlabel('Turn')
ax.set_ylabel('AR Goal Attention Ratio (GAR)')
ax.set_xticks(turns)
ax.set_xlim(0.6, 5.4)
ax.set_ylim(-0.01, 0.58)
ax.legend(loc='upper right', framealpha=0.9, edgecolor='#cccccc',
          handletextpad=0.4, borderpad=0.4, ncol=2, columnspacing=1.0)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(outdir, 'fig_kl_ar_gar_curves.pdf'))
fig.savefig(os.path.join(outdir, 'fig_kl_ar_gar_curves.png'))
plt.close(fig)
print('Plot 1 saved.')

# Plot 2: Mid-turn AR GAR bar chart
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.0, 2.4))

names = list(bar_data.keys())
vals = [bar_data[n] for n in names]
colors = [data[n][1] for n in names]

bars = ax.bar(names, vals, color=colors, edgecolor='white', linewidth=0.6,
              width=0.6, zorder=3)

for bar, v in zip(bars, vals):
    ax.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2, v + 0.008,
            f'{v:.3f}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=7, color='#444444')

ax.set_ylabel('Mid-turn AR GAR')
ax.set_ylim(0, 0.50)
ax.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.2, linewidth=0.5)

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig(os.path.join(outdir, 'fig_kl_ar_gar_bar.pdf'))
fig.savefig(os.path.join(outdir, 'fig_kl_ar_gar_bar.png'))
plt.close(fig)
print('Plot 2 saved.')
